title: Are You Sleeping - A Gentle Wake-Up Sing-Along for Toddlers
description: Morning bells are ringing! Stretch, clap and wake up with us. #kidssong #nurseryrhyme #toddlersongs #singalong #morningsong
characters: Three adorable Black toddlers: Zuri, a 3-year-old girl with deep warm brown skin, round afro puffs tied with soft yellow fabric scrunchies, wearing a sunny yellow t-shirt, denim dungaree shorts and white sneakers; Kofi, a 4-year-old boy with medium-deep brown skin, short dark natural curly hair, wearing a blue t-shirt, grey jogger shorts and red sneakers; and Nala, a 3-year-old girl with deep brown skin, neat cornrow braids, wearing a yellow pinafore dress over a white t-shirt, white tights and pink sneakers

lines: Are you sleeping, are you sleeping
verses.scene: Warm morning light falls across a cozy bedroom where a toddler is just stirring under a soft yellow blanket.

lines: Are you waking, are you waking
Clap your hands and stretch now
Clap your hands and stretch now
verses.scene: The toddlers sit up and stretch their arms wide above their heads, yawning and smiling in the sunny room.

lines: Clap and sing along with me
Ding dang dong, one, two, three
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together beside a little brass bell, counting on their fingers.

lines: Ding dang dong, ding dang dong
Clap your hands and sing along
Clap your hands and sing along
verses.scene: A small bright bell swings in a sunlit window while the toddlers sing along with their arms swinging.

lines: Clap and sing along with me
Ding dang dong, one, two, three
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together beside a little brass bell, counting on their fingers.

pd_source.text: Are You Sleeping (English text of 'Frere Jacques')
pd_source.author: Traditional (French, anonymous)
pd_source.publication: The French round is documented from the 18th century (manuscript c. 1780, printed in Paris collections from 1811); the standard English text is a 19th-century traditional translation.
pd_source.public_domain: Anonymous traditional text well over two centuries old; the English words are traditional and appear in 19th-century nursery collections. Long out of copyright everywhere.
pd_source.adaptation: Verse 1 is the traditional English text verbatim, re-lined into four lines with 'Morning bells are ringing' repeated as the source round does. 'Ding dang dong' is kept from the source. Verse 2 and the hook are NEWLY WRITTEN. The name 'Brother John' is kept — it is part of the public-domain text and is never depicted on screen.

song_style: children's nursery rhyme, gentle cheerful kids song, cute female child voice, simple very repetitive catchy melody, soft morning bells, slow bouncy tempo, warm
